subtitle: A shorter voyage in search of Clank

body: Ratchet & Clank Future: Quest for Booty is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 adventure, released on 21 August 2008. After Clank's disappearance in Tools of Destruction, Ratchet and Talwyn seek a way to contact the Zoni, following a lead connected to a legendary space pirate. The compact campaign places greater emphasis on exploration, puzzles and platforming than the surrounding games. Ratchet's wrench becomes more than a weapon, supplying practical ways to manipulate the island environments. The familiar hero enters a smaller story whose progress depends on handling the space around him as well as defeating its occupants.

The Omniwrench Millennium 12 can pick up objects and use a tether to alter parts of the environment. These interactions turn a blocked route into something to investigate rather than simply a place where another enemy wave must be cleared. Heliogrubs provide light in dark areas, adding another object whose handling changes what can be reached. Familiar weapons return from Tools of Destruction, but they share attention with those more deliberate tasks. The player reads the next room for a mechanism, movable object or source of light before deciding which tool should be used.

David Bergeaud composed the music for a release positioned between Tools of Destruction and the later continuation of Ratchet's search. Its pirate setting gives the short journey a clear local character while keeping the larger mystery unresolved. PlayStation Network distribution allowed the game to work at a more compact scale than the usual console adventure. That scale suits its emphasis on puzzles and physical interaction. Quest for Booty uses an established character and set of abilities to explore another rhythm, allowing a brief island journey to carry the continuing series forward without pretending to be its final destination.
